### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 2e4197c416e6d360c4802b693075b903d945d796
* **doc_path:** /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra/CLAUDE.md
* **affected_section:** Always Do These #19

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

CLAUDE.md "Always Do These" #19 documents the ~73-second ceiling that prevents long-running test commands from completing in the orchestrator. The rule should make explicit that this ceiling applies ONLY to the Claude Code Bash tool environment (the CLI runtime in which the orchestrator executes commands), and NOT to CI runners (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite, etc.) where job-level timeouts are measured in minutes to hours.

This distinction matters because agents reading the rule need to know whether it constrains design choices for CI work. Cold-install times of 60–90 seconds for Python deps in CI, multi-minute build steps, full-suite test runs in CI, etc. are all unremarkable in CI but would breach the ceiling if invoked from the Claude Code Bash tool.

#### Actual Behavior

The current rule text states:

> Never run \`make test-unit-only\` or \`make test-e2e\` as a full-suite validation command — these broad test commands exceed the ~73s tool timeout ceiling and will be killed mid-run (exit 144), producing spurious failures.

It does not explicitly distinguish the Claude Code Bash tool environment from CI runners. Concrete consequence observed during the brainstorm session for epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968 on 2026-04-30: the orchestrator and a feasibility reviewer both treated CI cold-install times of 60–90s as a ceiling-breach risk for the new Python module deps, which is a misapplication of the rule. CI deps install caching (actions/setup-python with cache: 'pip', or uv) is the standard mitigation and the ceiling is irrelevant in that environment.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **affected_doc:** CLAUDE.md
* **affected_rule:** Always Do These #19 (~73s ceiling)
* **proposed_fix:** Add a one-line clarification at the start of rule #19, e.g.: "This ceiling applies to the Claude Code Bash tool environment (where the orchestrator executes commands) — NOT to CI runners, which have minutes-to-hours job timeouts. Cold-install or full-suite work that would not fit the ceiling here is unremarkable in CI." Optionally cross-link to a discussion of CI dep caching patterns (actions/setup-python cache: 'pip', uv, container-baked envs).
* **detection:** if a future agent flags a CI-side install/build/test duration as a ceiling-breach risk in scrutiny output, that is the same misapplication.
data.title: [CLAUDE.md]: Always Do These #19 ~73s ceiling rule does not distinguish Claude Code Bash tool from CI runners -> agents misapply the rule to CI work and flag normal CI install/build durations as ceiling-breach risks
